source_text: Γεγένηταί τις ὀνόματι Νοητός, τῷ γένει Σμυρναῖος. Οὗτος εἰσηγήσατο αἵρεσιν ἐκ τῶν Ἡρακλείτου δογμάτων· οὗ διάκονος καὶ μαθητὴς γίνεται Ἐπίγονός τις τοὔνομα, ὃς τῇ Ῥώμῃ ἐπιδημήσας ἐπέσπειρε τὴν ἄθεον γνώμην. Ὧι μαθητεύσας Κλεομένης, καὶ βίῳ καὶ τρόπῳ ἀλλότριος τῆς ἐκκλησίας, ἐκράτυνε τὸ δόγμα, κατ᾿ ἐκεῖνο καιροῦ Ζεφυρίνου διέπειν νομίζοντος τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, ἀνδρὸς ἰδιώτου καὶ αἰσχροκερδοῦς· [ὃς] τῷ κέρδει προσφερομένῳ πειθόμενος συνεχώρει τοῖς προσιοῦσι τῷ Κλεομένει μαθητεύεσθαι, καὶ αὐτὸς ὑποσυρόμενος τῷ χρόνῳ ἐπὶ τα αὐτὰ ὥρμητο, συμβούλου καὶ συναγωνιστοῦ τῶν κακῶν ὄντος αὐτῷ Καλλίστου, οὗ τὸν βίον καὶ τὴν ἐφευρεθεῖσαν αἵρεσιν μετ᾿ οὐ πολὺ ἐκθήσομαι. Τούτων κατὰ διαδοχὴν διέμεινε τὸ διδασκαλεῖον κρατυνόμενον καὶ ἐπαῦξον διὰ τὸ συναίρεσθαι αὐτοῖς τὸν Ζεφυρῖνον καὶ τὸν Κάλλιστον, καίτοι ἡμῶν μηδέποτε συγχωρησάντων, ἀλλὰ πλειστάκις ἀντικαθεστώτων πρὸς αὐτοὺς καὶ διελεγξάντων καὶ ἄκοντας βιασαμένων τὴν ἀλήθειαν ὁμολογεῖν· οἳ πρὸς μὲν ὥραν αἰδούμενοι καὶ ὑπὸ τῆς ἀληθείας συναγόμενοι ὡμολόγουν, μετ᾿ οὐ πολὺ δὲ ἐπὶ τὸν αὐτὸν βόρβορον ἀνεκυλίοντο.
pass_a_gloss: There has become someone by name Noetus, by birth a Smyrnaean. This one introduced a heresy from the doctrines of Heraclitus; of whom a certain Epigonus becomes a deacon and disciple, who having arrived at Rome sowed the atheistic opinion. To whom Cleomenes, having become a disciple, and being a stranger to the church in life and manner, strengthened the doctrine, at that time when Zephyrinus was considered to preside over the church, a man who was a layman and lover of filthy lucre; who being persuaded by the gain offered to him permitted those coming to Cleomenes to become disciples, and himself being swept away by time rushed to the same things, Callistus being his counselor and fellow contender in evil, whose life and invented heresy I will set forth after a little. The teaching of these men remained strong through succession and increased because Zephyrinus and Callistus were gathering with them, although we never gave in to them, but many times stood against them and refuted them and forced them to confess the truth against their will; who for a time being ashamed and being constrained by the truth confessed, but after a little while returned to the same mire.
pass_b_english: A man named Noetus appeared, a native of Smyrna. He introduced a heresy drawn from the doctrines of Heraclitus. A certain Epigonus became his deacon and disciple; when Epigonus arrived in Rome he sowed the atheistic opinion there. Cleomenes became Epigonus’ disciple, and in both life and manner he was a stranger to the church. Cleomenes strengthened the doctrine at the time when Zephyrinus was considered to preside over the church. Zephyrinus was a layman and a lover of filthy lucre. Persuaded by the gain offered to him, Zephyrinus permitted those who came to Cleomenes to become disciples. Swept along by time, Zephyrinus himself rushed into the same errors, with Callistus as his counselor and fellow contender in evil. I will set forth Callistus’ life and his invented heresy shortly.

The teaching of these men remained strong through succession and increased, because Zephyrinus and Callistus were gathering with them. We, however, never gave in to them. Instead we stood against them many times, refuted them, and forced them to confess the truth against their will. For a time they confessed, ashamed and constrained by the truth, but after a little while they returned to the same mire.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex syntax of the Greek, particularly the nested clauses regarding Zephyrinus and the succession of the heretics. Pass B provides a clearer breakdown of the relationships (e.g., identifying Zephyrinus as the one swept by time) which is more faithful to the Greek structure than the more literal Pass A, while both remain faithful to the source.
